brief: Goldman's Pasquariello calls markets "metamorphic" after Thursday's 6.36% Nasdaq 100 drop (worst since Covid) and Friday's 165K payrolls, a 5-sigma beat that revived December hike odds; hedge fund losses round-tripped the year. He frames the outlook through three variables, all worsening on the margin. Earnings: S&P EPS grew 33% in Q2 and tracks 35% in Q3, the fastest pace in 30+ years outside recoveries, but is forecast to slow to 18% next year, and Goldman's model is highly sensitive to AI capex, whose risks rose this week. Flow of capital: hedge funds, households and corporates have all turned sellers since mid-August (HF net exposure lowest since March, AI-stock selling the fastest in 5+ years), and 2027 is forecast to bring the largest net equity supply increase since 2000 as IPOs (SpaceX, Anthropic) collide with corporates needing cash for capex over buybacks. AI narrative: big-five capex growth is seen slowing from 96% to 44% next year, hyperscalers burned $31bn in Q3 free cash flow, and Blue Wave data-center moratorium risk cuts both ways. His call: one last push higher, then a weaker, more volatile 2027; colleague Privorotsky argues the bullish 1998 case instead of 2000.
